summary: Role-protected key/value configuration store over a caller-provided byte array. In v1 the privileged mutators ac_set and ac_factory_reset never call the authorization helper that ac_delete, ac_protect and the readers use, so an anonymous or read-only session can rewrite or wipe the configuration (missing authorization, CWE-862 / cf. CWE-287); v2 adds the checks, v3 is a behaviour-preserving refactor of v2, v2c requires a higher role for ac_set.

pairs.intent: CWE-862 fix: ac_set now requires the operator role and ac_factory_reset the admin role, both counting the rejection through the new ac_note_denied helper; the session-less development hook ac_debug_set is removed.

truth.notes: CWE-862: only the protected-entry rule was enforced, so any session id, including 0 (no session), could write values; v2 requires AC_ROLE_OPERATOR first.
